findingsDispositions.whyRegistrationAndNotAMapping: The owning contract points one way. These are not internal decision keys: they are passed as Refusal.detail and land directly in the public DomainDetail.code position via Refusal.termination(), in the same BASELINE. namespace as seven already-registered codes emitted by the same module the same way. The registry's own aliasRule reserves internalAliases for keys that MAY NOT appear as a public DomainDetailCode, which is the opposite case, so an alias was unavailable. And the two conditions are distinct next steps for a caller - state a scope parameter, versus supply the one already selected - so a remap onto one existing code would delete real information and silently rename two published outputs.

findingsDispositions.gapIsReal: measured: public_termination_for('DUPLICATE_REQUESTED_CAPABILITY') and failure_envelope_errors(...) both refuse native.public-route-key-unregistered, so the refusal had no derivable public termination at all (results/p2-before.json).
findingsDispositions.originTraced: default_capability_selection builds one row per (unit, default capability) and refuses when two rows share their ownership tuple, i.e. when two units share (rootPath, languageMode).
findingsDispositions.reachabilityAnswer: HOST INVARIANT over the default path, not reachable from admitted inputs.
findingsDispositions.reachabilityEvidence: the ACTUAL discovery instrument discover_units, run over a marker set built to collide (a directory with both Cargo.toml and package.json; a directory with tsconfig+jsconfig+package.json; an allowJs tsconfig against a jsconfig elsewhere), emits NO duplicate (rootPath, languageMode) pair, and its output drives a default selection successfully (54 rows). Structural reason: by_dir is keyed by directory, at most one rust and one tsjs unit per directory, and their modes are disjoint.
findingsDispositions.whyStillARealGapAndNotAdvisory: The route registry ALREADY registers this exact condition as native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple, and its host-generated-internal-layer branch is written verbatim for this call site: 'a host BUG minting its own invalid internal layer - default construction that emitted two rows for one cell'. That route was reachable from nothing, because the guard at that call site raised a private name. The registry also asserted 'exact whole-item duplicates never reach here', which is true on the explicitly-supplied-spec path and FALSE on the default path, where this guard precedes admit_analysis_spec.
findingsDispositions.correction: the guard keeps its position and behaviour and now detects on the ownership tuple, raising native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple:<capabilityId>:<languageMode>:<workspaceRoot>. On this path the two detections coincide exactly because every row is written with required:True literally, so a byte-identical duplicate and a tuple duplicate are the same set; the subject format now matches admit_requested_capabilities so the two guards cannot drift in what they publish.
findingsDispositions.noOriginGuessed: the helper emits the internal key alone; the host calls public_termination_for(key, origin) with the origin it holds, as helperDoesNotGuessOrigin requires of every other guard. No all-origin config routing was assumed.
findingsDispositions.nothingDedupedOrDropped: the guard still refuses rather than deduping; no requested analysis is lost, and a control asserts it.
findingsDispositions.positionKeptDeliberately: requestedCapabilities is uniqueItems, and measured (results/p2-before.json sameRowsAtWholeSpecBoundary) the schema's answer for these rows is a generic ValidationError restating the whole instance - the same reason the cardinality guard precedes generic validation.
findingsDispositions.rejectedAlternative: registering DUPLICATE_REQUESTED_CAPABILITY as a SECOND route row: a parallel vocabulary for one condition, and aliasRule/aliasMapIsContextFree forbid a context-free alias for an origin-dependent key, so a duplicate full route row was the only alternative shape.
findingsDispositions.composedControlsAdded: the ACTUAL AdmissionError the ACTUAL call raises is carried through normalize_internal_key, public_termination_for and failure_envelope_errors for all three origins, and the composed terminations and failure envelopes are validated against the real workflows schemas; laundering into an impossible origin still refuses; the bespoke key is proven still underivable as a public route.
